annotations.title: Transfigured.
annotations.text: <mn>◦</mn> Marke in this Transfiguration many maruelous points. as, that he made not only his owne body, which then was mortal, but alſo the bodies of Moyſes and Elias, the one dead, the other to die, for the time as it were immortal: thereby to repreſent the ſtate and glorie of his body and his Saincts in heauen. By which maruelous transfiguring of his body, you may the leſſe maruel that he can exhibite his body vnder the forme of bread and vvine or otherewiſe as he liſt.

notes.text: Chriſt can exhibite his body vnder what forme he liſt.

annotations.title: Appeared Moyſes.
annotations.text: ◦ By this that Moyſes perſonally appeared and was preſent with Chriſt, it is plaine that the Saincts departed may in perſon be preſent at the affaires of the liuing. Auguſt. de cura pro mort. c. 15. 16. For euen as Angels els where, ſo here the Saincts alſo ſerued our Sauiour: and therfore as Angels both in the old Teſtament and the new, were preſent often at the affaires of men, ſo may Saincts.

notes.text: Saincts after their death deale with and for the liuing.

annotations.title: Mount.
annotations.text: [1] This mount (commonly eſteemed and named of the ancient Fathers Thabor) S. Peter [2] calleth the holy Mount becauſe of this wonderful viſion, like as in the old Teſtament where God appeared to Moyſes in the buſh, and elſewhere to others, he calleth the place of ſuch Apparitions, holy ground [3]. Whereby it is euident that by ſuch Apparitions, places are ſanctified, and therevpon groweth a religion and deuotion [4] in the faithful toward ſuch places, and namely to this Mount Thabor (called in S. Hierom Itabirium Ep. 17. ) there was great Pilgrimage in the Primitiue Church, as vnto al thoſe places which our Sauiour had ſanctified with his preſence and miracles, and therfore to the whole land of promis, for that cauſe called the holy land [5]. See. S. Hiero. in Epitap. Paulæ. & ep. 17. & 18. ad Marcellam.

notes.text: Deuotion and Pilgrimage to the ſame.

annotations.title: Elias ſhal come.
annotations.text: He diſtinguiſheth here plainly betwene <mn>[1]</mn> Elias in perſon, who is yet to come before the iudgement: and betwene Elias in name, to wit, Iohn the Baptiſt, who is come already in the ſpirit and vertue of Elias. <mn>[2]</mn>So that it is not Iohn Baptiſt only nor principally of whom Malachie prophecieth (as our Aduerſaries ſay) but Elias alſo him ſelf in perſon.

annotations.title: Why could not we.
annotations.text: <mn>[1]</mn> No maruel if the Exorciſts of the Catholike Church which haue power to caſt out diuels, yet doe it not alwaies when they wil, and many times with much a doe: Wheras the Apoſtles hauing receiued this power <mn>[2]</mn> before ouer vncleane ſpirites, yet here cannot caſt them out. But as for hæretikes, they can neuer doe it, nor any other true miracle, to confirme their falſe faith.

notes.text: True miracles only in the Cath. Church.

annotations.title: Faith as muſtard ſeed.
annotations.text: This is the Catholike faith, by which only al miracles are wrought: yet not of euery one that hath the Catholike faith, but of ſuch as haue a great and forcible faith, and withal the gift of miracles. Theſe are able as here wee ſee by Chriſtes warrant not only to doe other wonderful miracles here ſignified by this one, but alſo this very ſame, that is, to moue mountaines in deede, as S. Paul <mn>[1]</mn> alſo preſuppoſeth, and S. Hierom <mn>[2]</mn> affirmeth, and Eccleſiaſtical hiſtories namely telleth of <mn>[3]</mn> Gregorius Neocæſarienſis, that he moued a mountaine to make roome for the foundation of a Church, called therfore and for other his wonderful miracles, Thaumaturgus. And yet faithleſſe Heretikes laugh at al ſuch things aud beleue them not.

notes.text: Hiero. in vita S. Hilarionis. Niceph. li. 6. c. 17. Greg. Niſs. de vit. Gregorij.

annotations.title: Prayer and faſting.
annotations.text: <mn>◦</mn> The force of faſting and praying: whereby alſo we may ſee that the holy Churche in Exorciſmes doeth according to the Scriptures, when ſhee vſeth beſide the name of <sc>IESVS</sc>, many prayers and much faſting to driue out Deuils, becauſe theſe alſo are here required beſide faith.

annotations.title: The Children free.
annotations.text: Though Chriſt to auoid ſcandal, payed tribute, yet indeed he ſheweth that both himſelf ought to be free from ſuch payments (as being the kings ſonne, as well by his eternal birth of God the Father, as temporal of Dauid) and alſo his Apoſtles, as being of his familie, and in them their ſucceſſors the whole Clergie, who are called in Scripture the lotte and portion of our Lord. ◦ Which exemption and priuilege being grounded vpon the very law of nature itſelf, and therfore practiſed euen among the Heathen (Gen. 42, 27.) good Chriſtian Princes haue confirmed and ratified by their lawes, in the honour of Chriſt, whoſe miniſters they are, and as it were the kings ſonnes, as S. Hierom declareth playnly in theſe wordes, We for his honour pay not tributes, and as the Kings ſonnes, are free from ſuch payments. Hiero. vpon this place.

notes.text: The priuileges and exemptions of the Clergie.

annotations.title: Me and thee.
annotations.text: ◦ A great myſterie in that he payed not only for himſelf, but for Peter bearing the Perſon of the Churche, and in whom as the cheefe, the reſt were conteyned. Aug. q. ex no. Teſt. q. 75. to. 4.
